summary: v7.1 is internally legible (auto-merged from 10 section drafts) but exhibits systematic cross-milestone contradictions on controller scope, JM fleet realities, CAM tier-1 set, AI hierarchy, and a stale 35-vs-38 stage post pipeline number that build-vision flags as a still-open gap. MS-PILOT cites machines that do NOT exist in the JM Die fleet declared in MS-MASTERPOST, breaking the train/pilot grounding promise.

findings.issue: MS-PILOT phases P2-P5 are scoped on Haas-TM-1P-2008, Mori-Seiki-SL-3-1998, Bridgeport-1985, Haas-VF-2-2015, Mazak-QT-200-2012, Doosan-DNM-4500-2018, Mazak-Integrex. NONE of these (except Haas VF-2) appear in the JM Die 15-machine fleet table in MS-MASTERPOST (which lists Okuma GENOS L300/L200E/LNC8/Crown L1060/L400II/LB 3000EX/Multus B250II, Okuma M460V-5AX, Hurco VM30i, Haas VF-2, Haas OM-2, Roku-Roku HC 658-II, Mitsubishi EA12S/EA12D/FA10S). MS-PILOT is validating on a phantom fleet.

findings.loc: MS-TRAIN L1675-1680 vs MS-PILOT L1920 vs MS-MASTERPOST L1489-1493
findings.issue: MS-TRAIN trains on 6 controllers (Hurco WinMAX / Okuma OSP family / Mitsubishi W31MV-2 wire EDM / Haas PRE-NGC / Fanuc 31i-B5 / Mitsubishi FP80S+C30EA-2 sinker). MS-PILOT acceptance asserts byte-equivalence on 'Haas NGC, Fanuc 31i, Mazatrol Smooth G, OSP-P300' — Mazatrol is NOT in the MS-TRAIN training set and is explicitly listed P2/Post-MVP in MS-MASTERPOST priority table. PILOT therefore gates on a controller TRAIN never trained.

findings.loc: MS-MASTERPOST L1489-1496 vs build-vision JM-fleet doctrine
findings.issue: Controller priority order Hurco→Haas PRE-NGC→Fanuc 31i-B5→Okuma harden→Mitsubishi sinker is plausible against the 21-machine ShopConfig BUT contradicts CLAUDE-BRIEF.md which calls Okuma B250IIW the 'flagship' (4/5 OSP support, 75% OSP-P300SA dialect, missing $1/$2 channels). Roku-Roku HC 658-II uses Fanuc 31i-B5 (per L1477) which is row #3 in priority, yet Roku-Roku is never named anywhere as a beneficiary — orphan machine.

Build-vision lists 4 open Master Post gaps: lead-in/out stub, build-quality-aware feed ceiling stub, 35-vs-38-stage pipeline number conflict, no E2E test for per-block adaptive S/F. v7.1 MS-MASTERPOST acceptance does NOT require resolving any of these. The 35/38 stage conflict, the per-block adaptive S/F E2E test, and the lead-in/out unit are absent from the 40 MP units. v7.1 ships Master Post 'productization' while leaving its top differentiator (per-block adaptive S/F per build-vision L75) unverified.

Build-vision declares SIX tier-1 CAM bridges: Fusion360, hyperMILL, Mastercam, Esprit, Inventor HSM, SolidWorks. v7.1 MS-MASTERPOST parser unit list covers Fusion (P0), Mastercam (P1), hyperMILL (P1), Esprit/SolidCAM (P2 — and SolidCAM is NOT a tier-1 bridge, it is tier-2 per CLAUDE-BRIEF), Inventor HSM (absent from parser list, only mentioned in narrative L1441), SolidWorks (absent). Two of six tier-1 CAMs have NO parser unit. SolidCAM has been silently smuggled into tier-1.

findings.loc: L1475 (Multus B250II) vs L614 (B250IIW) vs build-vision L207/216 (B250IIW / next-action #19)
findings.issue: MS-MASTERPOST L1475 names the flagship 'Multus B250II' (without W suffix); MS2 U-INV-LATHE-04 L614 uses 'B250IIW'. Build-vision §jm_fleet doctrine explicitly mandates the rename to B250IIW because filesystem header confirms the 'W' (sub-spindle variant). v7.1 has not propagated the rename — re-introduces the legacy name in the launch-beachhead table.

Header claims '37 customer pages + 9 backend-prereq + 4 stub-remediation + 5 net-new engine + 5 hoist-wiring + 1 billing-concurrency = 61 units total'. Reconciliation line L165 says '6 SFC + 5 mill + 5 lathe + 7 WEDM + 4 quality + 7 ADMIN + 3 learn = 37 customer pages. Plus 18 backend prereq + hoist + remediation units = 61 total'. The header partitions 9+4+5+5+1=24 backend; the recon partitions 18. Both cannot be correct against a single 61 total — 24 backend leaves 37 customer (consistent), 18 backend leaves 43 customer (inconsistent with the same line's own '37'). Off-by-6 in the canonical count.

Inventor HSM has no parser unit despite being tier-1 saleable (build-vision §cam_bridges). The narrative L1441 lists it among supported uploads. Either drop it from supported uploads or add a U-REV-MP-XX Inventor HSM parser unit. Same for SolidWorks CAM.

Three controllers marked 'MISSING — build in MS-TRAIN' (Haas PRE-NGC P1, Fanuc 31i-B5 P0-external, Mitsubishi sinker P1) but the MS-MASTERPOST 4-week MVP critical path (L1591) does NOT depend on these engines, and they are not enumerated as U-TRAIN-XX build units in §8 L1803. The 'build in MS-TRAIN' promise has no unit referent.

Build-vision flags a NAMED canonical Tier-2 coordinator gap (4 fragmented candidates: PRISMUnifiedOrchestrator, AISystemRouter, MetaAIOrchestration, AIIntelligenceMaximizer; next-action #9 builds PRISMSystemCoordinatorEngine). v7.1 contains no unit building this canonical coordinator. With 16 of 17 Tier-3 AIs lacking working feedback loops (per brief), shipping subscription tiers (MS1) and live pilot (MS-PILOT) without the Tier-2 supervision contract is a coherence break — system can sell premium 'fit' tiers it cannot calibrate.

MS-TRAIN designs lathe_lora rank-8, okuma_operator_lora rank-4, mitsubishi_sinker_lora rank-4 trained on JM Die archive. CLAUDE-BRIEF observes '0 .safetensors / .pt / .gguf adapters anywhere on disk despite 80 LoRA support engines referencing them'. v7.1 does NOT include a unit to produce the FIRST adapter file on disk before designing the cadence — the cadence layer is grafted onto scaffolding the brief calls textbook-scaffold-without-loop.

Merges of mcp-cadquery frontend (CadViewer3DPage) and cqask/ui (NL→CadQueryPage) are required for revenue surfaces but no merge plan / port collision strategy / React version alignment is referenced. CLAUDE-BRIEF cites '2 frontend merges pending'. v7.1 builds on top of unresolved merges.

100% byte-equivalence vs JM Die golden NC is asserted as P-1 acceptance for Master Post. The JM Die archive is explicitly labeled 'noisy training data, NOT gold-standard' (CLAUDE-BRIEF L127, PRISM-BUILD-CONTEXT corpus reality). Byte-equivalence to noisy data is the wrong acceptance criterion — coherence break between corpus policy and pilot gate. Use motion-plan equivalence (which §6 L1568 already names) instead.

Build-vision flags 'Master post for Haas (master_post_haas_*) is missing despite 2 production Haas mills — next-action #8'. v7.1 MS-MASTERPOST builds Haas PRE-NGC emitter (U-REV-MP-10 P0) — good — but the engine name in MS-TRAIN L1678 is 'MISSING — build in MS-TRAIN' without specifying engine identity, while MS-MASTERPOST treats the emitter as a parser/emitter unit not an engine build. Two paths describe the same gap incompatibly.

findings.loc: MS0 U-REV-MS0-ACT-WEDM-CTRL-01 L54 vs MS2 L560
findings.issue: MS0 lists 5 WEDM dialects: Mitsubishi/Sodick/Makino/AgieCharmilles/Fanuc. MS2 L560 says '5 dialects already wired (Mitsubishi/Sodick/Makino/Agie/Fanuc post engines + DialectRouter)'. Consistent. BUT MS-MASTERPOST controller priority (L1489) names only Mitsubishi sinker (W31MV-2 + FP80S/C30EA-2) and never references Sodick/Makino/AgieCharmilles in the launch path despite MS0 wiring them as P1. Either v7.1 is over-wiring WEDM dialects vs the launch beachhead, or the sales/training plan is silently dropping 3 WEDM controllers.
